files.note: first_name: ternary rewritten as early-return guard. `if not rows` is the exact negation of the old `if rows`, so empty/None -> None and otherwise rows[0]["name"] are unchanged. No other callers in the repo.
New one-line note stating the refactor must not change documented contracts; consistent with AGENTS.md. It is the standard for judging permissions.py.

can_edit: tuple membership replaced by set-literal membership. Tuple `in` uses ==; set `in` requires hashing, so an unhashable role (list/dict) now raises TypeError instead of returning False, contradicting the AGENTS.md contract that any other role returns False. No callers exist in the repo, so real role types are unknown.

findings.trigger: can_edit is called with an unhashable role value such as a list or dict (e.g. a list of roles).
findings.effect: Set membership hashes the operand, so it raises TypeError instead of returning False as the AGENTS.md contract requires for any other role. The base tuple used == comparison and returned False.
findings.fix: Restore the tuple (or otherwise keep a non-hashing comparison); a two-element membership gains nothing from a set.
findings.refutation: No callers in the repo, so unhashable inputs are not shown to occur; roles are probably strings. Severity is kept at P3 for that reason. The contract says 'any other role' and the change is declared behavior-preserving, so the regression is attributable to the target.
findings.comment: role이 list나 dict처럼 해시할 수 없는 값이면 set 멤버십 검사에서 TypeError가 납니다. 기존 튜플은 False를 반환했고 AGENTS.md도 그 외 role은 False라고 정의합니다. 두 값 비교라 set의 이점이 없으니 튜플로 되돌려 주세요.
